review_candidates.description: The Department of Earth Sciences at Stellenbosch University invites applications for a two-year Postdoctoral Research Fellowship, funded by DSTI-NRF CIMERA, at the interface of economic geology, mineral systems science and thermodynamic modelling. The research will focus on gold metallogeny in sub-Saharan Africa. Through its multiple Wilson cycles, the amalgamation of the sub-Saharan landmass (the Kalahari, Congo and Tanzania cratons) provides a natural laboratory for investigating how ore-forming processes have operated through time. Yet gold metallogeny across the region remains fragmented, with tectonic setting, fluid sources, host-rock properties, alteration signatures and deposition mechanisms described inconsistently from one terrane to the next. This project will first synthesise these observations through a critical, data-driven meta-analysis of sub-Saharan gold deposits, and then test whether the key ore-forming processes can be parameterised on a thermodynamic footing and embedded within 3D/4D tectonic models. The goal is a process-based model for assessing gold prospectivity that supports next-generation, lower-impact exploration. The Fellow will work within an active research group linked to the ARM Chair in Geometallurgy and the IGCP-UNESCO West Congo Belt project, alongside regional gold metallogeny experts (Tanzania, DRC, Namibia and Mozambique) and international thermodynamic and fluid-chemistry modelling collaborators.
